value: few individuals in crepuscular periods and highest abundances in the morning and in the afternoon
method: autonomous programmable rotating video systems filming wild fish hourly from dusk to dawn over several days; abundance per count by size class and behaviour
conditions: Wild Mediterranean rainbow wrasse in coralligenous habitat on the French Riviera; filmed in situ, not held. The abstract names two study areas (not named in the abstract) and states the significant hour-scale variability in C. julis abundances for one of the two areas only. These differences were mainly due to small and medium C. julis, low in crepuscular periods, whereas large-sized individuals were equally abundant during the day. Crepuscular periods were associated with sudden changes of abundances and behaviour (more mobile and solitary individuals, few feeding individuals); feeding occurred mainly in the morning. The measure is abundance per video count, not tracked activity. The paper calls the species diurnal. The other species studied (Diplodus vulgaris) is not filed here.

source.authors: Witkowski F, Vion A, Bouchoucha M
